chapter: Other bands: Royal Jazz, H&J, Rainbow Room
title: Six or seven years at the H&J; Blue and Wendell Eugene
summary: He stayed with bands a long time, spent six or seven years at the H&J with Jacques Pierre, Emma Barris and trumpeter Blue, whose place Wendell Eugene took.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Most of the bands you've played with, you've been there quite some time, haven't you?

Yes. Yeah, I stayed with them a good while. You stayed with the band. I wasn't the kind that we even quit, you know. I always try to get along with those, you know. So I always try to stick, play with them as long as the band's going. Yeah, now at the H&J, well, we had a pretty good band there. I've stood there, what, six, seven years, I think, at the H&J.
Were there that long? I didn't know you were there.

You didn't know, man. No, you sure didn't. And Amir Rowdy, you knew him? Yeah, I didn't know him. Emma Barris, she was playing there. Emma Barris was there? Yeah, Emma Barris was there. She was there when I heard you.
You don't remember who else was there?
No, Jacques Pierre, he played drums. And a boy called Blue. That boy should have been the best trumpet player in town.
I don't know him, but I've heard of him.
Yeah, that's all I've been knowing about. Blue, they tell me his daddy was a trumpet player, Walter Blue, years ago.
Oh, Blue would probably be his last name then, huh?

That's right, yeah. His daddy was named Walter Blue. And so he might be Walter Blue, he could be a junior. Well that boy was playing some trumpet down there until Uncle Sam called him in to go to war. And guess what I got to play trumpet in his place? I got Wendell Eugene who played trumpet on the trombone. Oh, yeah. And he did a wonderful job.
Oh, he played his trombone but played the trumpet part.
